identifier_policy: VG:SCHOLAR: and VG:SWORK: are new deterministic prefixes of the same shape as the existing VG:WORK: and VG:CLAIM: identifiers. No existing identifier is proposed for change, no random id is used, and no ScholarlyWork is given a VG:WORK: identifier -- doing so would change what every per-Veda denominator means, which is the hazard GAP-SCHOLARSHIP-002 names.

new_labels.Commentator: A second label on a Scholar who is a traditional commentator, so a query can separate the commentarial layer from the philological one without a string test on a name.
new_labels.Interpretation: One attributed position about one passage: asserter, work, locator, claim, verbatim source quote. This is the node the relations connect.
new_labels.Scholar: A named person or a named corporate asserter of a scholarly or commentarial position. Carries scholar_type and attribution_status, because "Sayana of the Atharvaveda" is an ascription the reporting source itself disputes and the graph must be able to say so.
new_labels.ScholarlyWork: A work in which a position is stated. Distinct from :Work, which addresses the four Samhitas: a ScholarlyWork is never part of the corpus denominator and must not be given a VG:WORK: identifier.

new_relationship_types.REPORTED_BY: (:Interpretation)-[:REPORTED_BY]->(:ScholarlyWork) -- the work in which we read the position, where that is not the work that holds it. 9 of the 11 works here were not read directly, and the graph must not lose that.

CONTRADICTS.decision: Reuse CONTRADICTS rather than mint a synonym, because two relationship types meaning "these disagree" is how an attribution axis ends up with three disagreeing writers. But every edge MUST carry disagreement_scope, and the two existing edges must be backfilled to disagreement_scope=CROSS_CATEGORY_METHODOLOGICAL before any of these rows are imported.
CONTRADICTS.existing_semantics: The existing pair is NOT two rival readings of the Vedic text. VG:CLAIM:SV-IDENTITY-IS-MELODIC says so in its own about_basis: "the pair is a CROSS-CATEGORY methodological disagreement about what textual overlap implies, not two rival readings of the Vedic text".
CONTRADICTS.measured_before_reuse: CALL db.relationshipTypes() lists CONTRADICTS, and it carries exactly 2 edges, which are one bidirectional pair between VG:CLAIM:SV-IDENTITY-IS-MELODIC and VG:CLAIM:SV-PREDOMINANTLY-RV-REUSE, both :InterpretiveClaim. Their properties are knowledge_layer=L4_INTERPRETIVE_CLAIM, evidence_basis=STRUCTURAL, attribution_precision=NOT_AN_ATTRIBUTION, quality_tier=TIER_D.

required_properties_on_every_new_edge.disagreement_axis: one of the axis values enumerated in axes_used below

CONTRADICTS.why_the_backfill_is_not_optional: Without it, the product question "what do scholars disagree about here?" would return the Samaveda melodic-identity pair as though it were an attributed scholarly disagreement. It is this project's own reading against this project's own measurement, and neither side has a named asserter: asserted_by is the empty string on all 6 existing :InterpretiveClaim nodes. That is the exact failure GAP-SCHOLARSHIP-001 describes, and importing on top of it would hide rather than close it.
